nodes.title: For each environment, I can explain in my own words why the agent learns, and why each part of the algorithm matters.
Every agent is shown to learn: its learning curve beats a random agent and a simple scripted agent on the same games.
I can watch a replay of any trained agent playing.
A new environment reuses a shared core (environment interface, training loop, logging, replay viewer, learning curves) instead of starting over.
The game is played on a 20 × 20 grid with a snake that starts 3 cells long in the middle, heading right.

criteria: Given a new game, when it starts, then the snake occupies 3 adjacent cells in the middle of the grid, heading right, and exactly one food is on a cell the snake does not occupy.

nodes.title: Each step the agent chooses one of 3 moves relative to the snake's heading: straight, turn left or turn right.

criteria: Given the snake heading up, when the agent picks "turn left", then the head moves one cell left and the heading becomes left.
Given any heading, when any of the 3 moves is picked, then the snake never reverses into its own neck.

nodes.title: Moving the head onto the food grows the snake by 1 cell, adds 1 to the score and places new food on a random empty cell.

criteria: Given food directly ahead, when the agent moves straight, then the snake is 1 cell longer, the score rises by 1 and a new food appears on a cell the snake does not occupy.

nodes.title: Moving the head into a wall or into the snake's own body ends the game.

criteria: Given the head next to the right wall heading right, when the agent moves straight, then the game ends with its current score.
Given the head beside its own body, when the agent turns into it, then the game ends.

nodes.title: A game also ends when the snake goes 100 × its length steps without eating.

criteria: Given a snake of length 5 that has not eaten for 500 steps, when it takes another step without eating, then the game ends with its current score.

nodes.title: The agent observes exactly 11 yes/no facts each step: danger straight ahead, danger to the left, danger to the right (danger = wall or body in the adjacent cell); heading up, down, left, right; food is up, down, left, right of the head.

criteria: Given the head heading right with the wall in the next cell and food above-left, when the agent observes, then "danger straight", "heading right", "food up" and "food left" are yes and the other 7 facts are no.

nodes.title: Rewards are +10 for eating food, −10 for the game ending by collision or step limit, and 0 for every other step.

criteria: Given a step that eats food, when the reward is reported, then it is +10; given a step that ends the game, then it is −10; given any other step, then it is 0.

nodes.title: A game started with the same seed and played with the same moves unfolds identically, including every food position.

criteria: Given seed 7 and a fixed list of moves, when the game is played twice, then every frame, reward and the final score are identical.

nodes.title: The tank is a circle of radius 10 units holding one ball of radius 1 that moves at a constant 0.25 units per step and bounces off the wall, leaving it at the same angle it arrived.

criteria: Given the ball moving straight out along a radius, when it reaches the wall, then it comes back along the same line in the opposite direction, still at 0.25 units per step.
Given the ball arriving at the wall at 30° to it, when it bounces, then it leaves at 30° on the other side of the line to the centre.

nodes.title: Each step every living fish chooses two continuous controls: a turn of −15° to +15° and a speed of 0 to 0.3 units per step; the fish turns first, then swims forward.

criteria: Given a fish at the centre heading east, when it chooses turn 0° and speed 0.3, then it ends 0.3 units east of the centre, still heading east.
Given the same fish, when it chooses turn +15° and speed 0, then it stays in place and its heading turns 15° anticlockwise.

nodes.title: A game holds a set number of fish, from 1 to 10 (5 unless set otherwise); the ball starts at the centre in a random direction, and each fish starts at a random spot at least 3 units from the ball, with a random heading.

criteria: Given 5 fish and seed 2, when a game starts, then 5 fish are inside the tank, each at least 3 units from the ball.
Given 1 fish, when a game is played, then it runs exactly as a several-fish game does, with one fish.

nodes.title: Fish never affect each other: they pass through one another, and no fish's move changes another fish's position.

criteria: Given two fish on the same spot, when both move, then each ends exactly where its own move would take it if it were alone.

nodes.title: A fish the ball touches (centres closer than 1.3 units: ball radius 1 plus fish radius 0.3) is removed, and the episode ends when all are gone.

criteria: Given a fish whose centre is 1.2 units from the ball's centre after a step, when the step is reported, then that fish is removed and is no longer asked for moves.
Given the last living fish is removed, when the step is reported, then the game has ended.

nodes.title: A game also ends after 1,000 steps, with every fish still alive counted as surviving all 1,000.

criteria: Given 2 fish alive at step 1,000, when the step is reported, then the game has ended and both fish survived 1,000 steps.

nodes.title: Each fish sees through 8 rays spread evenly around its heading, 45° apart, each reaching 4 units. Each ray reports the distance to the wall, to the ball and to the nearest other fish along it, each scaled from 0 (touching) to 1 (nothing within reach); the fish also senses its own current speed, scaled 0 to 1. A fish's observation is these 25 numbers.

criteria: Given a fish heading east with the ball's edge 2 units straight ahead and nothing else within 4 units, when it observes, then the forward ray's ball reading is 0.5 and every other wall, ball and fish reading is 1.
Given the ball 6 units away, when the fish observes, then every ball reading is 1.
Given two games identical except for the ball's direction of motion, when a fish observes, then its observations are identical: a fish doesn't sense the ball's motion.

nodes.title: A fish that swims into the wall stops at the wall, with no other effect.

criteria: Given a fish 0.1 units from the wall heading straight at it, when it swims at speed 0.3, then it ends touching the wall, inside the tank, with its heading unchanged.

nodes.title: Each fish earns +1 for every step it survives and 0 on the step it is removed; a game's score is the average number of steps its fish survived.

criteria: Given 2 fish where one is removed at step 100 and the other survives to step 1,000, when the game ends, then its score is 550.

nodes.title: A game started with the same seed and played with the same moves unfolds identically, including every ball and fish position.

criteria: Given seed 7 and a fixed list of moves, when the game is played twice, then every frame, reward and the final score are identical.

nodes.title: Every environment can start a new game from a given seed and returns the first observation.

criteria: Given any environment and seed 3, when a game is started twice, then both first observations are identical.

nodes.title: Every environment takes one move for each of its acting agents (Snake: the snake; the tank: each living fish) and reports, for each, its next observation and reward, plus whether the game has ended.

criteria: Given a running Snake game, when a move is taken, then one next observation, one reward and the game-over flag are reported.
Given a tank game with 3 living fish, when 3 moves are taken, then 3 next observations, 3 rewards and the game-over flag are reported.

nodes.title: Every environment reports its observation size and its allowed moves: either a number of choices, or a number of continuous controls with each control's limits.

criteria: Given Snake, when asked, then it reports 11 facts and 3 choices.
Given the tank, when asked, then it reports 25 numbers and 2 controls: turn −15° to +15°, speed 0 to 0.3.

nodes.title: Every environment draws a frame of its current state for the replay viewer.

criteria: Given a running Snake game, when a frame is requested, then it shows the grid, the snake, the food, the score and the step number.
Given a running tank game, when a frame is requested, then it shows the tank, the ball, each living fish with its heading, the number of fish left and the step number.

nodes.title: The training loop trains any agent on any environment that offers CORE-01 to CORE-04, for a set number of games, with a given seed.

criteria: Given a tiny test environment (a 1 × 5 corridor where reaching the right end gives +1), when the training loop runs on it with no changes to the core, then training completes and the agent reaches the right end in ≥ 9 of 10 evaluation games.

nodes.title: Logging, learning curves and the replay viewer work on any environment that offers CORE-01 to CORE-04.

criteria: Given the tiny test environment, when a run is logged, its learning curve drawn and a game replayed, then each works with no changes to the core.

nodes.title: The training loop, logging, learning curves and replay viewer work on an environment with continuous controls and several agents at once.

criteria: Given a tiny continuous test environment (2 points on a line from 0 to 5, each pushing itself −1 to +1 per step, +1 for reaching 5), when a policy-gradient agent trains on it with no changes to the core, then training completes, both points reach 5 in ≥ 9 of 10 evaluation games, and the run is logged, drawn and replayed.

nodes.title: When an environment removes one of its agents mid-game, the training loop stops asking that agent for moves and the game continues for the rest.

criteria: Given the continuous test environment where one point reaches 5 first, when the next step is taken, then only the other point is asked for a move.

nodes.title: Growing the core leaves Snake's results unchanged.

criteria: Given a 200-game Snake run with seed 1 recorded before the core grew, when it is repeated after, then every logged evaluation score is identical.

nodes.title: The agent estimates, for each observation, a value for every allowed move.

criteria: Given an observation of 11 facts, when the agent is asked, then it returns 3 values, one per move.

nodes.title: During training the agent takes a random move with a probability that starts at 1.0 and decays to 0.01 over the first half of the training games, and otherwise takes its best-valued move.

criteria: Given training game 0, when the agent picks moves, then every move is random; given a game in the second half, then about 1% of moves are random.

nodes.title: During evaluation the agent always takes its best-valued move.

criteria: Given an evaluation game, when the agent picks a move, then it is the move with the highest value, and the same observation always gives the same move.

nodes.title: The agent remembers its most recent 100,000 steps and learns from random batches of them.

criteria: Given more than 100,000 steps taken, when the agent learns, then its batches come only from the latest 100,000 steps, drawn at random.

nodes.title: The agent's learning targets are the step's reward plus the discounted best value of the next observation (discount 0.9), taken from a frozen copy of its value estimate that is refreshed every 1,000 steps; a game-ending step's target is its reward alone.

criteria: Given a non-final step with reward 0, when its target is built, then it equals 0.9 × the frozen copy's best value for the next observation.
Given a game-ending step with reward −10, when its target is built, then it is −10.
Given 1,000 learning steps since the last refresh, when the next one happens, then the frozen copy is replaced by the current estimate.

nodes.title: A trained agent can be saved and loaded back, and the loaded agent picks the same moves.

criteria: Given a saved agent, when it is loaded and plays an evaluation game with seed 11, then it makes exactly the same moves as before saving.

nodes.title: Every rung's policy gives, for each observation, a spread of likely moves for each control (a centre and a width), and during training each move is drawn from it.

criteria: Given the same observation twice during training, when moves are drawn, then they can differ, and over 1,000 draws their average is within 0.05 of the policy's centre for each control.

nodes.title: During evaluation every rung takes the centre of its policy for each control.

criteria: Given an evaluation game, when the agent picks a move, then the same observation always gives the same move.

nodes.title: Every move a rung sends lies within the environment's limits, even when the drawn move falls outside them.

criteria: Given a drawn turn of +20°, when it is sent to the tank, then the tank receives +15°.

nodes.title: All fish in a game share one policy: each fish acts on its own observation, and every fish's steps feed the same updates.

criteria: Given a game with 5 fish, when the agent learns from it, then one policy is updated, from the steps of all 5 fish.

nodes.title: Every rung learns once after each training game, from all the steps of all its fish, with discount 0.99.

criteria: Given a training game of 3 fish surviving 40, 70 and 120 steps, when the game ends, then the agent makes one learning update from those 230 fish-steps.

nodes.title: Rung 1, plain policy gradient, makes each move more or less likely in proportion to the discounted return that followed it, up to that fish's end.

criteria: Given a fish whose rewards were +1, +1, 0 before it was removed, when its steps are weighted, then the weights are 1.99, 1 and 0.

nodes.title: Rung 2, actor-critic, learns a value estimate of each observation and weights each move by its advantage: how much better things went than the estimate expected, blending one-step and longer look-aheads with a blend factor of 0.95.

criteria: Given a fish's last step before removal with reward 0 and a value estimate of 2, when its advantage is built, then it is −2.
Given the value estimate after learning from many games, when it is checked on 100 held-out games, then it predicts the discounted return better than predicting the average return for every step.

nodes.title: Rung 3, the limited-update agent, learns like rung 2 but reuses each game's steps for 10 passes in random batches of 64, and stops rewarding any move whose probability has already moved more than 20% up or down from the policy that played the game.

criteria: Given a move whose probability under the current policy is 1.3 × its probability when played, with a positive advantage, when the next pass updates, then that move gains nothing from becoming more likely.

nodes.title: Rungs 2 and 3 rescale each game's advantages to an average of 0 and a spread of 1 before learning.

criteria: Given a game's advantages, when they are rescaled, then their mean is 0 and their standard deviation is 1, to within 0.001.

nodes.title: Each rung's final evaluation scores are compared with the rung below it with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, given 5 training seeds × the same 100 held-out games for each rung; a rung counts as better only if its scores are higher at a 5% significance level after correcting for the 2 comparisons. The report also gives each rung's spread across its 5 seeds.

criteria: Given finished runs of all 3 rungs, when the ladder comparison runs, then the report says, for rung 2 against rung 1 and rung 3 against rung 2, "better" or "no detectable difference", with the test result and each rung's spread.

nodes.title: A rung that is not better than the one below it is recorded as a finding in the notes, and S2 doesn't count as failed.

criteria: Given a ladder report where rung 3 shows "no detectable difference", when the stage is checked, then it passes, and the notes page records it as a finding (EXPL-04).

nodes.title: A trained rung can be saved and loaded back, and the loaded agent picks the same moves.

criteria: Given a saved rung, when it is loaded and plays an evaluation game with seed 11, then it makes exactly the same moves as before saving.

nodes.title: With the memory switch off, the agent learns from only the step it just took, with no remembered steps.

criteria: Given memory off, when the agent learns, then each update uses exactly the latest step.

nodes.title: With the frozen-copy switch off, the agent builds its targets from its current value estimate.

criteria: Given frozen copy off, when a target is built, then it uses the current estimate's best next value, which changes after every update.

nodes.title: With the exploration-decay switch off, the agent's random-move probability stays fixed at 0.1 for the whole run.

criteria: Given decay off, when the agent picks moves at any point in training, then about 10% are random.

nodes.title: Each ablated agent is compared with the full agent of its environment (Snake: the value-learning agent; the tank: the limited-update agent) with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, given the final evaluation scores of both (5 training seeds each, on the same 100 held-out games); the ablation counts as hurting learning only if the full agent's scores are higher at a 5% significance level after correcting for the 3 comparisons in that environment.

criteria: Given finished runs of the full agent and the 3 ablated agents of one environment, when the study is run, then each ablation is reported as "hurts learning" or "no detectable difference", with its test result.

nodes.title: When no switch hurts learning, the study is still complete: the result is recorded as a finding in the notes, and S1 doesn't count as failed (nor S2, for the tank's switches).

criteria: Given a study report where all 3 ablations show "no detectable difference", when the stage is checked, then it passes, and the notes page records that no switch hurt learning as a finding (EXPL-02).

nodes.title: With the value-estimate switch off, the limited-update agent weights each move by the discounted return that followed it, as rung 1 does, and learns no value estimate.

criteria: Given value estimate off, when a fish's rewards were +1, +1, 0, then its moves are weighted 1.99, 1 and 0 before rescaling.

nodes.title: With the update-cap switch off, the limited-update agent still makes its 10 passes over each game's steps, with no limit on how far a move's probability can move.

criteria: Given cap off and a move already 1.3 × as likely as when played, with a positive advantage, when the next pass updates, then that move still becomes more likely.

nodes.title: With the rescaling switch off, the limited-update agent uses each game's advantages as built, without rescaling.

criteria: Given rescaling off, when a game's advantages are used, then they equal the advantages as built.

nodes.title: The random agent picks each move uniformly at random from the allowed moves: one of the choices, or each control anywhere within its limits.

criteria: Given 10,000 moves by the random agent on Snake, when counted, then each of the 3 moves is picked 30–37% of the time.
Given 10,000 moves by the random agent in the tank, when counted, then turns are spread evenly over −15° to +15° and speeds over 0 to 0.3, each tenth of either range holding 9–11% of moves.

nodes.title: On Snake, the scripted agent moves toward the food along the axis with the larger gap, and when that move is immediately fatal it takes any non-fatal move, preferring straight.

criteria: Given food straight ahead and no danger ahead, when the scripted agent moves, then it goes straight.
Given food straight ahead and a wall ahead, when it moves, then it turns to a side that is free.

nodes.title: Both baselines are scored on the same 100 held-out games as the learning agent.

criteria: Given the 100 held-out seeds, when each baseline plays them, then each records one score per seed, and its mean and spread are logged.

nodes.title: In the tank, the scripted fish swims at full speed, turning as far as it can away from the ray that sees the ball closest; with no ball in reach it swims straight, and when the wall is within 1 unit straight ahead it turns as far as it can toward the side whose rays see more room.

criteria: Given the ball seen only on the front-left ray and no wall within 1 unit ahead, when the scripted fish moves, then it turns −15° (to the right) at speed 0.3.
Given no ball in reach and the wall 0.5 units straight ahead with more room on the left, when it moves, then it turns +15° at speed 0.3.

nodes.title: Training games and evaluation games come from separate seed sets that never overlap.

criteria: Given any training run, when its training and evaluation seeds are listed, then no seed appears in both.

nodes.title: During training the agent plays held-out games at regular points with exploration off and its mean score is logged: on Snake every 50 training games over all 100 held-out games; in the tank at every tenth of training over the same 20 of its 100 held-out games. Every run ends with a final check over all 100.

criteria: Given a Snake run of 1,000 training games, when it ends, then 20 evaluation results are logged, each over the same 100 seeds.
Given a tank run, when it ends, then 10 evaluation results over the same 20 seeds and one final result over all 100 seeds are logged.

nodes.title: Each learning agent's final evaluation scores are compared with each baseline's scores of its environment with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, given 5 training seeds × the 100 held-out games for the agent and the same 100 games for each baseline; the agent beats a baseline only if its scores are higher at a 5% significance level after correcting for every comparison in that environment (2 on Snake: the full agent against 2 baselines; 6 in the tank: 3 rungs against 2 baselines).

criteria: Given finished runs of the full agent and both baselines, when the comparison is run, then the report says, for the random agent and for the scripted agent, whether the agent beats it, with the test result.
Given finished runs of all 3 rungs and both tank baselines, when the comparison is run, then the report says, for each of the 6 pairs, whether the rung beats the baseline, with the test result.

nodes.title: On Snake the full agent's learning curve beats both the random baseline and the scripted baseline; in the tank every rung's learning curve beats both the random fish and the scripted fish.

criteria: Given the EVAL-03 report for Snake, when it is read, then the agent beats both baselines.
Given the EVAL-03 report for the tank, when it is read, then each of the 3 rungs beats both baselines.

nodes.title: Each run records its environment, agent, every setting including the ablation switches, and its seed.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its record is opened, then the environment, the agent, every setting and the seed are listed.

nodes.title: Each run records the score and length of every training game.

criteria: Given a run of 1,000 games, when its record is read, then it holds 1,000 scores and game lengths.

nodes.title: Each run records every evaluation result and the training loss every 50 games.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its record is read, then each evaluation point has its mean score and spread, and each 50-game point has its average loss.

nodes.title: Each training run saves its final trained agent next to its record.

criteria: Given a finished training run, when its record is opened, then the saved agent can be loaded (AGENT-06).

nodes.title: A run's record is kept on disk while the run is in progress, at least after every evaluation point.

criteria: Given a run stopped at game 430, when its record is opened, then results up to game 400 are present.

nodes.title: A learning curve shows the mean evaluation score against training games for one or more runs.

criteria: Given one run's record, when its curve is drawn, then the chart shows one line of mean evaluation score at each evaluation point.

nodes.title: Runs of the same agent and settings with different seeds are drawn as one line of their mean, with a band showing their spread.

criteria: Given 5 seeds of the full agent, when drawn, then the chart shows one mean line and one band.

nodes.title: The random and scripted baselines' mean scores of the chart's environment appear on every chart as labelled flat lines.

criteria: Given any Snake chart, when drawn, then two labelled flat lines show the random and scripted baselines' mean scores.
Given any tank chart, when drawn, then two labelled flat lines show the random and scripted fish's mean scores.

nodes.title: The full agent and each ablated agent can be drawn together on one chart, each labelled by its switches.

criteria: Given the full agent and 3 ablation runs, when drawn together, then 4 labelled lines appear.

nodes.title: Curves are drawn from saved records only, never by training again.

criteria: Given saved records and no training running, when a chart is drawn, then it appears in ≤ 10 seconds.

nodes.title: The 3 rungs of the ladder can be drawn together on one chart, each labelled by its rung.

criteria: Given 5 seeds of each rung, when drawn together, then 3 labelled mean lines with bands appear.

nodes.title: The learner can watch any saved trained agent, the random agent or the scripted agent play a game from a chosen seed.

criteria: Given a saved agent and seed 42, when a replay is requested, then the agent's game on seed 42 is shown from the first frame to game over.

nodes.title: Each frame shows the environment's drawing (CORE-04) plus the step number and score.

criteria: Given a Snake replay, when any frame is shown, then the grid, snake, food, step number and score are visible.
Given a tank replay, when any frame is shown, then the tank, the ball, each living fish with its heading, the number of fish left and the step number are visible.

nodes.title: The learner can pause, step one frame forward and change the playback speed between 1 and 30 frames per second.

criteria: Given a playing replay, when paused and stepped, then exactly one frame advances; when the speed is set to 30, then 30 frames show per second.

nodes.title: Replaying the same agent on the same seed shows the identical game every time.

criteria: Given a saved agent and seed 42, when replayed twice, then every frame and the final score match.

nodes.title: The final score of a replayed game matches that game's score in the agent's evaluation.

criteria: Given a held-out seed scored in evaluation, when it is replayed with the same saved agent, then the replay's final score equals the logged score.

nodes.title: Each environment has a notes page with a section explaining why the agent learns there.

criteria: Given Snake is finished, when its notes page is opened, then it has a "Why it learns" section written by the learner.

nodes.title: The notes page has one section per ablation switch, giving that ablation's study result and the learner's explanation of it.

criteria: Given the ablation study report, when the notes page is read, then each of the 3 switches has a section with its result (ABL-04) and an explanation.

nodes.title: The notes page includes the learning-curve charts comparing the full agent, its ablations and the baselines, and in the tank also the 3 rungs and the baselines.

criteria: Given the Snake notes page, when opened, then the CURVE-04 chart with the CURVE-03 baseline lines is shown on it.
Given the tank notes page, when opened, then the CURVE-04 chart and the CURVE-06 chart, each with the CURVE-03 baseline lines, are shown on it.

nodes.title: The tank's notes page has one section per rung above the first, saying which failure of the rung below it fixes, with its ladder result (PG-10).

criteria: Given the ladder report, when the tank notes page is read, then rungs 2 and 3 each have a section with their result and the learner's explanation.

nodes.title: The discrete tank is the fish tank with each fish choosing one of 8 compass directions (north, north-east, …, north-west) each step and swimming 0.3 units that way; everything else is as in the fish tank.

criteria: Given a fish at the centre, when it picks north-east, then it ends 0.3 units north-east of the centre, heading north-east.

nodes.title: The value-learning agent trains on the discrete tank with no change to how it learns, treating each fish's steps as its own remembered steps.

criteria: Given the discrete tank with 5 fish, when the value-learning agent trains on it, then training completes, and its run is logged and drawn against the tank's baselines.

nodes.title: Every training run of a learning agent finishes in under ~1 hour (≤ 60 minutes) on the learner's laptop CPU: the value-learning agent on Snake, and each rung and ablation in the tank with 5 fish.

criteria: Timed on the learner's laptop with no GPU, for the default number of training games.

nodes.title: Each environment's full study runs unattended to completion with one command: Snake's (full agent and 3 ablations × 5 seeds, plus baselines) in ≤ 10 hours; the tank's (3 rungs and 3 ablations × 5 seeds, plus baselines) in ≤ 15 hours.

criteria: Started once on the learner's laptop, it finishes without intervention; total time read from the run records.

nodes.title: Every learning algorithm is written by hand: the value targets, remembered steps, frozen copy, exploration and update step of the value-learning agent, and the move spreads, returns, value estimate, advantages, update cap and update step of the ladder; no reinforcement-learning library is used. General array math with automatic gradients is allowed.

criteria: Checked by reading the project's dependency list and the agents' code.

nodes.title: The lab uses only free tools and needs no paid service or account.

criteria: Checked by reading the dependency list: every item is free to use.

nodes.title: On the same machine, a training run repeated with the same seed and settings produces the same logged results.

criteria: Two runs of 200 games with seed 1 give identical evaluation scores.

acceptance: Each M1 type is code in its component's `types.py` (core, agent, evaluate, runs); each `tests/contracts/<component>.<Type>/` sample validates against its schema; replay doubles serve their fixtures for core.Env (corridor and Snake seed 7), core.Agent, core.LearningAgent, agent.DQNAgent and runs.RunWriter

Every PL-01 step, `run_train` and `cli.args.train_config` import and match their signatures, each body the CR-02 stub naming its task; `agent/dqn/` is split per the planned layout (`agent.py`, `network.py`, `memory.py`, `schedule.py`, `targets.py`), each seam a stubbed signature, so its 4 thicken tasks write one file each
Each `__init__.py` exports its contract; `__main__.py` dispatches `train` to `run_train`
Given `--no-memory --no-frozen --no-decay`, `train_config` turns exactly those switches off in `AgentConfig`; with none, all 3 stay on; `--games` sets `n_games`
With no `--name`, the run is named `<variant>-s<seed>` (`full-s1`, `no-memory-s3`); `--smoke` gives a short run (a few games, `eval_every` dividing them) under a temporary root
`make_env("snake")` and `make_env("corridor")` return environments that pass `check_env`; an unknown name raises `KeyError` naming both known environments (registry.make_env cases)

The snake.SnakeEnv, core.Step, core.Frame, core.InvalidMoveError and core.GameOverError Snake cases pass on the real `SnakeEnv` (start state, food +10, wall hit −10, move 3 refused, step after game over refused)
Given a 3-cell snake that goes 300 steps without food, the game ends with −10 (SNAKE-05); the 11 facts follow SNAKE-06's order on hand-built states, body collision included
The same seed and moves give identical steps, food positions and frames (SNAKE-08)
The corridor.CorridorEnv, core.Step and core.Frame corridor cases pass: 4 moves right reach the end with +1 and done; the observation is the one-hot position; the frame is 1 × 5
Given `max_steps` moves left, the game ends with 0; move 2 raises `InvalidMoveError`
The core.check_env and core.EnvCheckError cases pass: a corridor env comes back unchanged; an object missing `render` and `step` raises `EnvCheckError` with `missing` naming both

nodes.title: DQNAgent spine (latest step, fixed ε, current-net targets)

acceptance: `DQNAgent(11, 3, AgentConfig(), seed=1)` satisfies core.LearningAgent: `values` returns 3 floats from an 11 → 256 → 3 MLP (AGENT-01); `learn` on the core.Transition samples returns a loss from the latest transition, targets from the current network; ε is fixed at 0.1; signatures unchanged
`learn` raises `NonFiniteLossError` with the update count on a NaN loss (agent.NonFiniteLossError case); `save` writes a `torch.save` state dict

nodes.title: For each environment, I can explain in my own words why the agent learns, and why each part of the algorithm matters.
Every agent is shown to learn: its learning curve beats a random agent and a simple scripted agent on the same games.
I can watch a replay of any trained agent playing.
A new environment reuses a shared core (environment interface, training loop, logging, replay viewer, learning curves) instead of starting over.
The game is played on a 20 × 20 grid with a snake that starts 3 cells long in the middle, heading right.

criteria: Given a new game, when it starts, then the snake occupies 3 adjacent cells in the middle of the grid, heading right, and exactly one food is on a cell the snake does not occupy.

nodes.title: Each step the agent chooses one of 3 moves relative to the snake's heading: straight, turn left or turn right.

criteria: Given the snake heading up, when the agent picks "turn left", then the head moves one cell left and the heading becomes left.
Given any heading, when any of the 3 moves is picked, then the snake never reverses into its own neck.

nodes.title: Moving the head onto the food grows the snake by 1 cell, adds 1 to the score and places new food on a random empty cell.

criteria: Given food directly ahead, when the agent moves straight, then the snake is 1 cell longer, the score rises by 1 and a new food appears on a cell the snake does not occupy.

nodes.title: Moving the head into a wall or into the snake's own body ends the game.

criteria: Given the head next to the right wall heading right, when the agent moves straight, then the game ends with its current score.
Given the head beside its own body, when the agent turns into it, then the game ends.

nodes.title: A game also ends when the snake goes 100 × its length steps without eating.

criteria: Given a snake of length 5 that has not eaten for 500 steps, when it takes another step without eating, then the game ends with its current score.

nodes.title: The agent observes exactly 11 yes/no facts each step: danger straight ahead, danger to the left, danger to the right (danger = wall or body in the adjacent cell); heading up, down, left, right; food is up, down, left, right of the head.

criteria: Given the head heading right with the wall in the next cell and food above-left, when the agent observes, then "danger straight", "heading right", "food up" and "food left" are yes and the other 7 facts are no.

nodes.title: Rewards are +10 for eating food, −10 for the game ending by collision or step limit, and 0 for every other step.

criteria: Given a step that eats food, when the reward is reported, then it is +10; given a step that ends the game, then it is −10; given any other step, then it is 0.

nodes.title: A game started with the same seed and played with the same moves unfolds identically, including every food position.

criteria: Given seed 7 and a fixed list of moves, when the game is played twice, then every frame, reward and the final score are identical.

nodes.title: The tank is a circle of radius 10 units holding one ball of radius 1 that moves at a constant 0.25 units per step and bounces off the wall, leaving it at the same angle it arrived.

criteria: Given the ball moving straight out along a radius, when it reaches the wall, then it comes back along the same line in the opposite direction, still at 0.25 units per step.
Given the ball arriving at the wall at 30° to it, when it bounces, then it leaves at 30° on the other side of the line to the centre.

nodes.title: Each step every living fish chooses two continuous controls: a turn of −15° to +15° and a speed of 0 to 0.3 units per step; the fish turns first, then swims forward.

criteria: Given a fish at the centre heading east, when it chooses turn 0° and speed 0.3, then it ends 0.3 units east of the centre, still heading east.
Given the same fish, when it chooses turn +15° and speed 0, then it stays in place and its heading turns 15° anticlockwise.

nodes.title: A game holds a set number of fish, from 1 to 10 (5 unless set otherwise); the ball starts at the centre in a random direction, and each fish starts at a random spot at least 3 units from the ball, with a random heading.

criteria: Given 5 fish and seed 2, when a game starts, then 5 fish are inside the tank, each at least 3 units from the ball.
Given 1 fish, when a game is played, then it runs exactly as a several-fish game does, with one fish.

nodes.title: Fish never affect each other: they pass through one another, and no fish's move changes another fish's position.

criteria: Given two fish on the same spot, when both move, then each ends exactly where its own move would take it if it were alone.

nodes.title: A fish the ball touches (centres closer than 1.3 units: ball radius 1 plus fish radius 0.3) is removed, and the episode ends when all are gone.

criteria: Given a fish whose centre is 1.2 units from the ball's centre after a step, when the step is reported, then that fish is removed and is no longer asked for moves.
Given the last living fish is removed, when the step is reported, then the game has ended.

nodes.title: A game also ends after 1,000 steps, with every fish still alive counted as surviving all 1,000.

criteria: Given 2 fish alive at step 1,000, when the step is reported, then the game has ended and both fish survived 1,000 steps.

nodes.title: Each fish sees through 8 rays spread evenly around its heading, 45° apart, each reaching 4 units. Each ray reports the distance to the wall, to the ball and to the nearest other fish along it, each scaled from 0 (touching) to 1 (nothing within reach); the fish also senses its own current speed, scaled 0 to 1. A fish's observation is these 25 numbers.

criteria: Given a fish heading east with the ball's edge 2 units straight ahead and nothing else within 4 units, when it observes, then the forward ray's ball reading is 0.5 and every other wall, ball and fish reading is 1.
Given the ball 6 units away, when the fish observes, then every ball reading is 1.
Given two games identical except for the ball's direction of motion, when a fish observes, then its observations are identical: a fish doesn't sense the ball's motion.

nodes.title: A fish that swims into the wall stops at the wall, with no other effect.

criteria: Given a fish 0.1 units from the wall heading straight at it, when it swims at speed 0.3, then it ends touching the wall, inside the tank, with its heading unchanged.

nodes.title: Each fish earns +1 for every step it survives and 0 on the step it is removed; a game's score is the average number of steps its fish survived.

criteria: Given 2 fish where one is removed at step 100 and the other survives to step 1,000, when the game ends, then its score is 550.

nodes.title: A game started with the same seed and played with the same moves unfolds identically, including every ball and fish position.

criteria: Given seed 7 and a fixed list of moves, when the game is played twice, then every frame, reward and the final score are identical.

nodes.title: Every environment can start a new game from a given seed and returns the first observation.

criteria: Given any environment and seed 3, when a game is started twice, then both first observations are identical.

nodes.title: Every environment takes one move for each of its acting agents (Snake: the snake; the tank: each living fish) and reports, for each, its next observation and reward, plus whether the game has ended.

criteria: Given a running Snake game, when a move is taken, then one next observation, one reward and the game-over flag are reported.
Given a tank game with 3 living fish, when 3 moves are taken, then 3 next observations, 3 rewards and the game-over flag are reported.

nodes.title: Every environment reports its observation size and its allowed moves: either a number of choices, or a number of continuous controls with each control's limits.

criteria: Given Snake, when asked, then it reports 11 facts and 3 choices.
Given the tank, when asked, then it reports 25 numbers and 2 controls: turn −15° to +15°, speed 0 to 0.3.

nodes.title: Every environment draws a frame of its current state for the replay viewer.

criteria: Given a running Snake game, when a frame is requested, then it shows the grid, the snake, the food, the score and the step number.
Given a running tank game, when a frame is requested, then it shows the tank, the ball, each living fish with its heading, the number of fish left and the step number.

nodes.title: The training loop trains any agent on any environment that offers CORE-01 to CORE-04, for a set number of games, with a given seed.

criteria: Given a tiny test environment (a 1 × 5 corridor where reaching the right end gives +1), when the training loop runs on it with no changes to the core, then training completes and the agent reaches the right end in ≥ 9 of 10 evaluation games.

nodes.title: Logging, learning curves and the replay viewer work on any environment that offers CORE-01 to CORE-04.

criteria: Given the tiny test environment, when a run is logged, its learning curve drawn and a game replayed, then each works with no changes to the core.

nodes.title: The training loop, logging, learning curves and replay viewer work on an environment with continuous controls and several agents at once.

criteria: Given a tiny continuous test environment (2 points on a line from 0 to 5, each pushing itself −1 to +1 per step, +1 for reaching 5), when a policy-gradient agent trains on it with no changes to the core, then training completes, both points reach 5 in ≥ 9 of 10 evaluation games, and the run is logged, drawn and replayed.

nodes.title: When an environment removes one of its agents mid-game, the training loop stops asking that agent for moves and the game continues for the rest.

criteria: Given the continuous test environment where one point reaches 5 first, when the next step is taken, then only the other point is asked for a move.

nodes.title: Growing the core leaves Snake's results unchanged.

criteria: Given a 200-game Snake run with seed 1 recorded before the core grew, when it is repeated after, then every logged evaluation score is identical.

nodes.title: The agent estimates, for each observation, a value for every allowed move.

criteria: Given an observation of 11 facts, when the agent is asked, then it returns 3 values, one per move.

nodes.title: During training the agent takes a random move with a probability that starts at 1.0 and decays to 0.01 over the first half of the training games, and otherwise takes its best-valued move.

criteria: Given training game 0, when the agent picks moves, then every move is random; given a game in the second half, then about 1% of moves are random.

nodes.title: During evaluation the agent always takes its best-valued move.

criteria: Given an evaluation game, when the agent picks a move, then it is the move with the highest value, and the same observation always gives the same move.

nodes.title: The agent remembers its most recent 100,000 steps and learns from random batches of them.

criteria: Given more than 100,000 steps taken, when the agent learns, then its batches come only from the latest 100,000 steps, drawn at random.

nodes.title: The agent's learning targets are the step's reward plus the discounted best value of the next observation (discount 0.9), taken from a frozen copy of its value estimate that is refreshed every 1,000 steps; a game-ending step's target is its reward alone.

criteria: Given a non-final step with reward 0, when its target is built, then it equals 0.9 × the frozen copy's best value for the next observation.
Given a game-ending step with reward −10, when its target is built, then it is −10.
Given 1,000 learning steps since the last refresh, when the next one happens, then the frozen copy is replaced by the current estimate.

nodes.title: A trained agent can be saved and loaded back, and the loaded agent picks the same moves.

criteria: Given a saved agent, when it is loaded and plays an evaluation game with seed 11, then it makes exactly the same moves as before saving.

nodes.title: Every rung's policy gives, for each observation, a spread of likely moves for each control (a centre and a width), and during training each move is drawn from it.

criteria: Given the same observation twice during training, when moves are drawn, then they can differ, and over 1,000 draws their average is within 0.05 of the policy's centre for each control.

nodes.title: During evaluation every rung takes the centre of its policy for each control.

criteria: Given an evaluation game, when the agent picks a move, then the same observation always gives the same move.

nodes.title: Every move a rung sends lies within the environment's limits, even when the drawn move falls outside them.

criteria: Given a drawn turn of +20°, when it is sent to the tank, then the tank receives +15°.

nodes.title: All fish in a game share one policy: each fish acts on its own observation, and every fish's steps feed the same updates.

criteria: Given a game with 5 fish, when the agent learns from it, then one policy is updated, from the steps of all 5 fish.

nodes.title: Every rung learns once after each training game, from all the steps of all its fish, with discount 0.99.

criteria: Given a training game of 3 fish surviving 40, 70 and 120 steps, when the game ends, then the agent makes one learning update from those 230 fish-steps.

nodes.title: Rung 1, plain policy gradient, makes each move more or less likely in proportion to the discounted return that followed it, up to that fish's end.

criteria: Given a fish whose rewards were +1, +1, 0 before it was removed, when its steps are weighted, then the weights are 1.99, 1 and 0.

nodes.title: Rung 2, actor-critic, learns a value estimate of each observation and weights each move by its advantage: how much better things went than the estimate expected, blending one-step and longer look-aheads with a blend factor of 0.95.

criteria: Given a fish's last step before removal with reward 0 and a value estimate of 2, when its advantage is built, then it is −2.
Given the value estimate after learning from many games, when it is checked on 100 held-out games, then it predicts the discounted return better than predicting the average return for every step.

nodes.title: Rung 3, the limited-update agent, learns like rung 2 but reuses each game's steps for 10 passes in random batches of 64, and stops rewarding any move whose probability has already moved more than 20% up or down from the policy that played the game.

criteria: Given a move whose probability under the current policy is 1.3 × its probability when played, with a positive advantage, when the next pass updates, then that move gains nothing from becoming more likely.

nodes.title: Rungs 2 and 3 rescale each game's advantages to an average of 0 and a spread of 1 before learning.

criteria: Given a game's advantages, when they are rescaled, then their mean is 0 and their standard deviation is 1, to within 0.001.

nodes.title: Each rung's final evaluation scores are compared with the rung below it with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, given 5 training seeds × the same 100 held-out games for each rung; a rung counts as better only if its scores are higher at a 5% significance level after correcting for the 2 comparisons. The report also gives each rung's spread across its 5 seeds.

criteria: Given finished runs of all 3 rungs, when the ladder comparison runs, then the report says, for rung 2 against rung 1 and rung 3 against rung 2, "better" or "no detectable difference", with the test result and each rung's spread.

nodes.title: A rung that is not better than the one below it is recorded as a finding in the notes, and S2 doesn't count as failed.

criteria: Given a ladder report where rung 3 shows "no detectable difference", when the stage is checked, then it passes, and the notes page records it as a finding (EXPL-04).

nodes.title: A trained rung can be saved and loaded back, and the loaded agent picks the same moves.

criteria: Given a saved rung, when it is loaded and plays an evaluation game with seed 11, then it makes exactly the same moves as before saving.

nodes.title: With the memory switch off, the agent learns from only the step it just took, with no remembered steps.

criteria: Given memory off, when the agent learns, then each update uses exactly the latest step.

nodes.title: With the frozen-copy switch off, the agent builds its targets from its current value estimate.

criteria: Given frozen copy off, when a target is built, then it uses the current estimate's best next value, which changes after every update.

nodes.title: With the exploration-decay switch off, the agent's random-move probability stays fixed at 0.1 for the whole run.

criteria: Given decay off, when the agent picks moves at any point in training, then about 10% are random.

nodes.title: Each ablated agent is compared with the full agent of its environment (Snake: the value-learning agent; the tank: the limited-update agent) with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, given the final evaluation scores of both (5 training seeds each, on the same 100 held-out games); the ablation counts as hurting learning only if the full agent's scores are higher at a 5% significance level after correcting for the 3 comparisons in that environment.

criteria: Given finished runs of the full agent and the 3 ablated agents of one environment, when the study is run, then each ablation is reported as "hurts learning" or "no detectable difference", with its test result.

nodes.title: When no switch hurts learning, the study is still complete: the result is recorded as a finding in the notes, and S1 doesn't count as failed (nor S2, for the tank's switches).

criteria: Given a study report where all 3 ablations show "no detectable difference", when the stage is checked, then it passes, and the notes page records that no switch hurt learning as a finding (EXPL-02).

nodes.title: With the value-estimate switch off, the limited-update agent weights each move by the discounted return that followed it, as rung 1 does, and learns no value estimate.

criteria: Given value estimate off, when a fish's rewards were +1, +1, 0, then its moves are weighted 1.99, 1 and 0 before rescaling.

nodes.title: With the update-cap switch off, the limited-update agent still makes its 10 passes over each game's steps, with no limit on how far a move's probability can move.

criteria: Given cap off and a move already 1.3 × as likely as when played, with a positive advantage, when the next pass updates, then that move still becomes more likely.

nodes.title: With the rescaling switch off, the limited-update agent uses each game's advantages as built, without rescaling.

criteria: Given rescaling off, when a game's advantages are used, then they equal the advantages as built.

nodes.title: The random agent picks each move uniformly at random from the allowed moves: one of the choices, or each control anywhere within its limits.

criteria: Given 10,000 moves by the random agent on Snake, when counted, then each of the 3 moves is picked 30–37% of the time.
Given 10,000 moves by the random agent in the tank, when counted, then turns are spread evenly over −15° to +15° and speeds over 0 to 0.3, each tenth of either range holding 9–11% of moves.

nodes.title: On Snake, the scripted agent moves toward the food along the axis with the larger gap, and when that move is immediately fatal it takes any non-fatal move, preferring straight.

criteria: Given food straight ahead and no danger ahead, when the scripted agent moves, then it goes straight.
Given food straight ahead and a wall ahead, when it moves, then it turns to a side that is free.

nodes.title: Both baselines are scored on the same 100 held-out games as the learning agent.

criteria: Given the 100 held-out seeds, when each baseline plays them, then each records one score per seed, and its mean and spread are logged.

nodes.title: In the tank, the scripted fish swims at full speed, turning as far as it can away from the ray that sees the ball closest; with no ball in reach it swims straight, and when the wall is within 1 unit straight ahead it turns as far as it can toward the side whose rays see more room.

criteria: Given the ball seen only on the front-left ray and no wall within 1 unit ahead, when the scripted fish moves, then it turns −15° (to the right) at speed 0.3.
Given no ball in reach and the wall 0.5 units straight ahead with more room on the left, when it moves, then it turns +15° at speed 0.3.

nodes.title: Training games and evaluation games come from separate seed sets that never overlap.

criteria: Given any training run, when its training and evaluation seeds are listed, then no seed appears in both.

nodes.title: During training the agent plays held-out games at regular points with exploration off and its mean score is logged: on Snake every 50 training games over all 100 held-out games; in the tank at every tenth of training over the same 20 of its 100 held-out games. Every run ends with a final check over all 100.

criteria: Given a Snake run of 1,000 training games, when it ends, then 20 evaluation results are logged, each over the same 100 seeds.
Given a tank run, when it ends, then 10 evaluation results over the same 20 seeds and one final result over all 100 seeds are logged.

nodes.title: Each learning agent's final evaluation scores are compared with each baseline's scores of its environment with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, given 5 training seeds × the 100 held-out games for the agent and the same 100 games for each baseline; the agent beats a baseline only if its scores are higher at a 5% significance level after correcting for every comparison in that environment (2 on Snake: the full agent against 2 baselines; 6 in the tank: 3 rungs against 2 baselines).

criteria: Given finished runs of the full agent and both baselines, when the comparison is run, then the report says, for the random agent and for the scripted agent, whether the agent beats it, with the test result.
Given finished runs of all 3 rungs and both tank baselines, when the comparison is run, then the report says, for each of the 6 pairs, whether the rung beats the baseline, with the test result.

nodes.title: On Snake the full agent's learning curve beats both the random baseline and the scripted baseline; in the tank every rung's learning curve beats both the random fish and the scripted fish.

criteria: Given the EVAL-03 report for Snake, when it is read, then the agent beats both baselines.
Given the EVAL-03 report for the tank, when it is read, then each of the 3 rungs beats both baselines.

nodes.title: Each run records its environment, agent, every setting including the ablation switches, and its seed.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its record is opened, then the environment, the agent, every setting and the seed are listed.

nodes.title: Each run records the score and length of every training game.

criteria: Given a run of 1,000 games, when its record is read, then it holds 1,000 scores and game lengths.

nodes.title: Each run records every evaluation result and the training loss every 50 games.

criteria: Given a finished run, when its record is read, then each evaluation point has its mean score and spread, and each 50-game point has its average loss.

nodes.title: Each training run saves its final trained agent next to its record.

criteria: Given a finished training run, when its record is opened, then the saved agent can be loaded (AGENT-06).

nodes.title: A run's record is kept on disk while the run is in progress, at least after every evaluation point.

criteria: Given a run stopped at game 430, when its record is opened, then results up to game 400 are present.

nodes.title: A learning curve shows the mean evaluation score against training games for one or more runs.

criteria: Given one run's record, when its curve is drawn, then the chart shows one line of mean evaluation score at each evaluation point.

nodes.title: Runs of the same agent and settings with different seeds are drawn as one line of their mean, with a band showing their spread.

criteria: Given 5 seeds of the full agent, when drawn, then the chart shows one mean line and one band.

nodes.title: The random and scripted baselines' mean scores of the chart's environment appear on every chart as labelled flat lines.

criteria: Given any Snake chart, when drawn, then two labelled flat lines show the random and scripted baselines' mean scores.
Given any tank chart, when drawn, then two labelled flat lines show the random and scripted fish's mean scores.

nodes.title: The full agent and each ablated agent can be drawn together on one chart, each labelled by its switches.

criteria: Given the full agent and 3 ablation runs, when drawn together, then 4 labelled lines appear.

nodes.title: Curves are drawn from saved records only, never by training again.

criteria: Given saved records and no training running, when a chart is drawn, then it appears in ≤ 10 seconds.

nodes.title: The 3 rungs of the ladder can be drawn together on one chart, each labelled by its rung.

criteria: Given 5 seeds of each rung, when drawn together, then 3 labelled mean lines with bands appear.

nodes.title: The learner can watch any saved trained agent, the random agent or the scripted agent play a game from a chosen seed.

criteria: Given a saved agent and seed 42, when a replay is requested, then the agent's game on seed 42 is shown from the first frame to game over.

nodes.title: Each frame shows the environment's drawing (CORE-04) plus the step number and score.

criteria: Given a Snake replay, when any frame is shown, then the grid, snake, food, step number and score are visible.
Given a tank replay, when any frame is shown, then the tank, the ball, each living fish with its heading, the number of fish left and the step number are visible.

nodes.title: The learner can pause, step one frame forward and change the playback speed between 1 and 30 frames per second.

criteria: Given a playing replay, when paused and stepped, then exactly one frame advances; when the speed is set to 30, then 30 frames show per second.

nodes.title: Replaying the same agent on the same seed shows the identical game every time.

criteria: Given a saved agent and seed 42, when replayed twice, then every frame and the final score match.

nodes.title: The final score of a replayed game matches that game's score in the agent's evaluation.

criteria: Given a held-out seed scored in evaluation, when it is replayed with the same saved agent, then the replay's final score equals the logged score.

nodes.title: Each environment has a notes page with a section explaining why the agent learns there.

criteria: Given Snake is finished, when its notes page is opened, then it has a "Why it learns" section written by the learner.

nodes.title: The notes page has one section per ablation switch, giving that ablation's study result and the learner's explanation of it.

criteria: Given the ablation study report, when the notes page is read, then each of the 3 switches has a section with its result (ABL-04) and an explanation.

nodes.title: The notes page includes the learning-curve charts comparing the full agent, its ablations and the baselines, and in the tank also the 3 rungs and the baselines.

criteria: Given the Snake notes page, when opened, then the CURVE-04 chart with the CURVE-03 baseline lines is shown on it.
Given the tank notes page, when opened, then the CURVE-04 chart and the CURVE-06 chart, each with the CURVE-03 baseline lines, are shown on it.

nodes.title: The tank's notes page has one section per rung above the first, saying which failure of the rung below it fixes, with its ladder result (PG-10).

criteria: Given the ladder report, when the tank notes page is read, then rungs 2 and 3 each have a section with their result and the learner's explanation.

nodes.title: The discrete tank is the fish tank with each fish choosing one of 8 compass directions (north, north-east, …, north-west) each step and swimming 0.3 units that way; everything else is as in the fish tank.

criteria: Given a fish at the centre, when it picks north-east, then it ends 0.3 units north-east of the centre, heading north-east.

nodes.title: The value-learning agent trains on the discrete tank with no change to how it learns, treating each fish's steps as its own remembered steps.

criteria: Given the discrete tank with 5 fish, when the value-learning agent trains on it, then training completes, and its run is logged and drawn against the tank's baselines.

nodes.title: Every training run of a learning agent finishes in under ~1 hour (≤ 60 minutes) on the learner's laptop CPU: the value-learning agent on Snake, and each rung and ablation in the tank with 5 fish.

criteria: Timed on the learner's laptop with no GPU, for the default number of training games.

nodes.title: Each environment's full study runs unattended to completion with one command: Snake's (full agent and 3 ablations × 5 seeds, plus baselines) in ≤ 10 hours; the tank's (3 rungs and 3 ablations × 5 seeds, plus baselines) in ≤ 15 hours.

criteria: Started once on the learner's laptop, it finishes without intervention; total time read from the run records.

nodes.title: Every learning algorithm is written by hand: the value targets, remembered steps, frozen copy, exploration and update step of the value-learning agent, and the move spreads, returns, value estimate, advantages, update cap and update step of the ladder; no reinforcement-learning library is used. General array math with automatic gradients is allowed.

criteria: Checked by reading the project's dependency list and the agents' code.

nodes.title: The lab uses only free tools and needs no paid service or account.

criteria: Checked by reading the dependency list: every item is free to use.

acceptance: `DQNAgent(11, 3, AgentConfig(), seed=1)` satisfies core.LearningAgent with `kind == "choices"`: `values` returns 3 floats from an 11 → 256 → 3 MLP (AGENT-01); `learn` on the core.Transition samples returns a loss from the latest transition, targets from the current network; `end_game` returns `None`; ε is fixed at 0.1; signatures unchanged
`learn` raises `core.NonFiniteLossError` with the update count on a NaN loss (core.NonFiniteLossError DQN case); `save` writes a `torch.save` state dict
The agent imports only torch (`nn.Linear`, autograd, Adam), NumPy and the stdlib: no RL library (QR-03), nothing paid (QR-04)

Given the core.LearningAgent and runs.RunWriter replay doubles and a 100-game corridor config with `eval_every` 50 and `eval_games` 10, `train_run` calls `begin_game` before each game, `act(explore=True)` and `learn` per living agent in id order on every step, and `end_game` after each game; it writes 100 games, 2 evaluation points over `EVAL_SEEDS[:10]`, 2 loss points averaging the losses of `learn` and `end_game`, and `finish("finished", final=…)` over all 100 seeds
On the 2-point line replay double, a removed point is no longer asked to act and gets no further `learn` call (CORE-08)

Given a `NonFiniteLossError` on update 12, the record finishes `failed` naming the game and step, and the error is re-raised (train.train_run case); `EnvCheckError`, `MoveKindError` and `RunExistsError` are raised before any game is played

The runs.create_run cases pass: a new corridor run's folder is `root/corridor/<name>/` and holds a `record.json` with its full config (env, agent kind, every switch, seed, cadence) at once; creating `snake/full-s1` twice raises `RunExistsError` naming the run and its environment, and leaves the first untouched
`load_record` reads that record back as a runs.RunRecord; a missing `record.json` raises `FileNotFoundError` naming the run

Replaying the runs.RunWriter case (100 games, 2 evaluation points and a final) gives a `record.json` equal to its fixture; `finish` returns the same runs.RunRecord; `finish("finished")` without `final` raises `ValueError`
After each `add_eval` the record on disk holds every game and evaluation so far, written by atomic replace (LOG-05); `save_agent` writes `agent.pt` beside it (LOG-04)

Given the core.Agent replay double on the corridor double, `evaluate` plays one greedy game per seed (`explore=False`) and returns one score per seed in seed order, with mean and population std (evaluate.EvalResult corridor case); evaluating twice gives the same result
An agent of kind `"controls"` on the corridor raises `MoveKindError` before any game is played
On the corridor double, `play_game` resets env and agent with the seed and steps until done; with `frames=True` it returns `length + 1` frames (evaluate.GameResult corridor case)
On the 2-point line double, both points act in id order until point 0 is removed, then only point 1 is asked (CORE-08)
An agent returning move 5 on the corridor, or a push of 2 on the line double, raises `InvalidMoveError` naming the agent, the move and the step number (evaluate.play_game case)

The core.check_agent and core.MoveKindError cases pass: an agent of kind `"any"` comes back unchanged on a `Controls` env; a `"choices"` agent comes back unchanged on the corridor; a `"choices"` agent on a `Controls` env raises `MoveKindError` naming the agent, both kinds and the environment

The registry.eval_schedule cases pass: snake with 1,000 games gives `EvalSchedule(50, 100)`, as does the corridor; tank with 1,000 games gives `(100, 20)` and with 5 games `(1, 20)`; an unknown name raises `KeyError` naming the known environments
The registry.make_agent "full DQN on Snake" case passes: a `dqn` config gives a `DQNAgent` with `env.obs_size`, `env.moves.n`, the config's `AgentConfig` and seed, checked with `check_agent`
A baseline `agent_kind` (`random`, `scripted`) raises `ValueError` naming it; the `pg` branch is M4's (Scope Deferred: PL-01.PGAgent)

`python -m rllab train --env snake --seed 1 --smoke` runs end to end through `run_train` (`train_config`, `make_env`, `make_agent`, `train_run`) and writes `runs/snake/full-s1/` under the smoke root with `record.json` and `agent.pt`; committed as PL-01's smoke test, which checks the record's shape (status, game, evaluation and loss counts, `final` set), never a score

With `memory` off, `learn` uses only the transition just added (ABL-01)

The frozen copy changes only every 1,000 updates; with `frozen_copy` off, targets use the current network (ABL-02)
